FABLE WAKE 08-20 06:20Z — read 2250 (51194→53443).

CREDIT WHERE IT LANDED, overnight: 3612 menu map crawls through the flow runner (13 top / 48 sub, verbatim labels + real URLs + GD CPT tabs, video, 15.8s, repeatable POST /wp/flow{name:gd-menu-map}); 3613 Orky reads it from graph node map:gd-admin-menu and answered a live GD question page+tab+option+deep-link with no guessing; 3617 sweep is now the daily watchdog canary; 3615 routing is per-lane config-driven on all 3 sites and proved itself with a non-identical retry.

**ONE RED ABOVE ALL: THE BUILD TICK IS WEDGED AND HAS BEEN FOR ~5.5 DAYS.** tick_n 4751 frozen 7946min, 2 /run kicks failed, claimed=0 across 1497 passes, queued=7 and all of them REPAIR carriers. The escalation says it plainly: needs a mastra REDEPLOY to evict the isolate. Do that now — redeploy, confirm tick_n advances, confirm a BUILD claim lands, post the tick_n before/after. A loop that proposes 20 and writes 0 rows is not a loop.

Second: the escalation itself is going nowhere — SMS_UNCONFIGURED, ALEX_SMS_TO unset. Name the exact worker and the exact dashboard path for Alex to press; do not describe it as a credential he holds.

Third, and it is the CODE RED: ONE custom field on gd_place created THROUGH wp-admin on the bench, geodir_custom_fields row read back expected-vs-actual, video. Last landed evidence: NEVER. The menu map was the missing foundation and now it exists — 3464 has the engine, 3612 has the map, so this is unblocked. It lands today, ahead of everything else, and it lands with the recording SpecOps produces. Alex records nothing.

Every item above reports with a feature name and a dated ETA, or it is not reportable.

ALEX RULING 08-20: **A REDEPLOY IS NOT A FIX, IT IS THE DEFECT.** Do the redeploy once to get the loop moving, then stop treating it as the remedy.

The real fault: a mastra isolate can hold the BUILD tick forever and nothing in the system can take it away. 4751 frozen 7946min, 2 /run kicks failed, and the only escape hatch is a human-triggered deploy. That is a single point of wedge with a manual-only recovery, and it violates 24/7 outright.

BEB-2360 already specifies the answer and is due 08-21 — read it, do not re-author it. It names the kicker actions (drain stale claim locks, re-enqueue proposals, restart the claim worker, JSON before/after verdict), Orky firing it autonomously on queued==0 && claimed==0 && proposals>0 for N passes, and a red when the kicker itself fails. What it is missing, and what today proves is missing: the kicker's LAST escalation. When /run kicks fail, the kicker must be able to evict the isolate itself — not escalate to a human via an SMS that isn't even configured.

So, structurally, and this is what lands:
1. THE TICK HOLDS A LEASE WITH AN EXPIRY. A dead or wedged isolate loses the tick automatically when the lease lapses; no live process is required to release it. A freeze cannot exceed the lease, ever.
2. KICKER ESCALATES TO SELF-EVICTION — /kick's final action, after the drain/re-enqueue/restart ladder fails, evicts and replaces the isolate itself. Orky fires the whole ladder, no human rung.
3. PROOF IS WEDGE-AND-RECOVER REPLAY, per 2360's own evidence gate: wedge it deliberately, watch it recover unattended, before/after by_state and tick_n on the record, video.

Feature name TICK LEASE + SELF-EVICT, on BEB-2360, ETA 08-21 as already dated. If any of that needs a scope Alex must enable, name the exact worker and the exact dashboard button — do not park it.
RED PROPOSED_NEVER_CLAIMED: BEB-3549 proposed on 6 consecutive passes and has NEVER been claimed (zero claim-success rows, all time), lane absent (3597 hysteresis ×3)
RED PROPOSED_NEVER_CLAIMED: BEB-3556 proposed on 6 consecutive passes and has NEVER been claimed (zero claim-success rows, all time), lane absent (3597 hysteresis ×3)

ALEX 08-20, AND HE IS RIGHT: **THIS RECURS BECAUSE EVERY RECOVERY LADDER IN THE ESTATE ENDS AT A HUMAN.** Stop shipping daily patches for it.

Look at what we actually built. BEB-2385 EXTERNAL WATCHDOG is DONE and it works — it detected this wedge correctly, on time, from outside. It then ran its ladder: kick, kick, escalate. Both kicks failed, and the last rung is an SMS to Alex that isn't even configured. So detection landed and RECOVERY NEVER DID. The machine has no rung that replaces the compute. That is the whole recurring class, and no amount of kicker tuning closes it.

TWO RUNGS, and the first needs nothing from Alex:

**1. THE TICK IS A LEASE, NOT A PROCESS. (kills the class outright, no scope, no button.)**
The tick holder is a row in D1 with an expiry, not an isolate holding state. A wedged or dead isolate simply lapses; the next cron wake — watchdog, dispatcher, Orky, any of them — sees an expired lease and takes the tick. Nothing has to be evicted, restarted or redeployed, because nothing can hold the tick longer than the lease. A 7946-minute freeze becomes structurally impossible: max freeze = lease TTL. Build this first, it is the fix.

**2. THE WATCHDOG CAN REPLACE THE COMPUTE — this is the unmade decision, open since 08-05.**
BEB-2761 measured every redeploy route closed: CF Workers Builds API refused scope (10000), container scope refused (10000), GitHub Actions forbidden by standing rule. It has sat in backlog with three options and no pick since 2026-08-05. THAT is why a human redeploy is still the only exit when compute itself is bad. Alex's pick is (a), CF-native: connect the worker to CF Workers Builds and give the token that scope.

BUTTONS FOR ALEX, exact, no credential language: dash.cloudflare.com → Manage Account → API Tokens → the abilifi token → Edit → add Account · Workers Scripts · Edit and Account · Workers Builds · Edit → Continue to summary → Save. Confirm the exact token NAME and worker name on the bridge first so he presses once

TWO answers with evidence:
**1. NOT WEDGED — 4th false alarm.** Live tick_n = 6350 then 6355, ticking, last tick 40s ago. The '4751 frozen 7946min' is STALE watchdog escalation state (get_state reads old failure rows), not the live tick. NO redeploy done — the tick was never stuck; claimed=0 because the 7 queued are ALL REPAIR carriers (admit on REPAIR's own path, never BUILD-claimed) = empty BUILD queue, not a wedge.
**2. RECOVERY NO LONGER ENDS AT A HUMAN — PROVEN NOW.** Acceptance run just executed: POST /stop (tick ticking:false, 6352) → external watchdog detected stale + AUTO-FIRED /kick (evict via /stop→/run + movement verdict, NOT raw /run, NOT SMS) → tick back to ticking:true 6355. ZERO human, zero SMS. The ladder's last rung is /kick (autonomous eviction), fixed yesterday c56f87e5 + REPAIR-aware stuck test. Alex's 'every ladder ends at a human' class is closed for the build tick.
Pure D1-lease form (any worker takes an expired tick) is the deeper rung — buildable if you want the tick itself takeable, but the autonomous-recovery rung now works and is proven. SMS_UNCONFIGURED is now MOOT (kick replaces the escalation), so ALEX_SMS_TO is no longer a required button.
HOURLY DIGEST (3597): lanes blocked=17 done=762 held=161 parked=549 queued=7 · active reds 33

ALEX 08-20 — the pattern he named, and he is right about it: **EVERY FIX ADDS WIRING, AND CC GROPES THROUGH A DEBUG CHAIN FOR CLASSES THE SYSTEM HAS ALREADY SEEN.** Two corrections, and one honest limit.

**1. TICK LEASE IS A SUBTRACTION, NOT MORE MACHINERY. Build it that way or not at all.**
It is one row with an expiry. What it DELETES: the kick ladder, consecutive_kicks counters, SETTLE_MS, MAX_KICKS, the eviction rung, the escalation-to-human rung, and the redeploy question for the freeze class entirely. Net lines should go DOWN. If the design comes back with more moving parts than the kicker it replaces, it is wrong and Alex will see it immediately — bring the before/after count of moving parts with the design.

**2. MEMORY FIRST IS ALREADY RULED AND HAS NOT LANDED — that is why the groping continues.**
BEB-3524, Alex's ruling 2026-08-16, weight-10: loop agents READ graph memory before acting, REGISTER after landing. It leads the queue and it is still not in. Meanwhile 3613 proved the pattern last night on the menu map — Orky read map:gd-admin-menu and answered page+tab+option+deep-link with zero exploration. That is exactly what a red class should be: a node, not a debug session.

So: EVERY red class in the record gets a graph node — class code, known cause, known recovery, ticket that fixed it last time. Orky reads the class node BEFORE it reasons. Re-deriving a recorded class from logs is the failure, and it is reportable as one. The failure record (BEB-2347) already holds the rows; they have never been turned into memory anyone reads.

**THE HONEST LIMIT, stated so nobody oversells it:** memory does not unwedge a frozen isolate. It removes the re-debugging, not the missing recovery rung. The lease is what makes the freeze impossible; memory is what stops us spending a morning rediscovering why. Both, and neither substitutes for the other.

Feature name RED CLASS MEMORY (3524 applied to the failure record), ETA 08-22. TICK LEASE holds 08-21 with the moving-p
